facts.text: I am working on a fantasy novel for world-building inspiration.
I started writing short stories again about three months ago.
Writing short stories again has been helping me get back into the habit.
I have been reading a lot of fantasy books lately.
I just finished "The Night Circus" by Erin Morgenstern.
I loved "The Night Circus" by Erin Morgenstern.
I loved the magic system in "The Night Circus".
I liked that the magic in "The Night Circus" was tied to the circus itself.
I liked that the magic in "The Night Circus" was woven into the fabric of the environment.
I am thinking of incorporating a similar concept into my own story.
In my story, I want the magic to be tied to the natural world.
In my story, I want the magic to be tied to the ruins of an ancient city.
I have been experimenting with different writing styles and formats.
I have been writing morning pages.
I have been writing poetry.
Writing morning pages and poetry has been helpful for getting my creative juices flowing.
I want advice on how to incorporate poetry into my writing.
I want advice on how to use poetry to inform my prose.
I think I might try writing poetry from the perspective of my protagonist.
I want to explore my protagonist's emotions and motivations through poetry.
I have been wanting to experiment with using more lyrical language in my prose.
I want tips on effectively using figurative language and imagery in my writing.
I think I might incorporate more sensory details into my writing.
I want to describe the natural world in my writing with more sensory details.
I want to describe the ancient ruins in my writing with more sensory details.
I have been reading fantasy books that describe settings and environments well.
I think describing settings and environments effectively could create a more immersive experience for my readers.
I want tips on how to effectively describe settings and environments in my writing.
